The orchestrator records the circuit-breaker failure but then unconditionally quality-scores the empty text and returns a normal GenerationResult. GenerationResult has no error/status field. worker/tasks.py:128-142 only counts raised exceptions as row errors, so error results become 'successful' rows. Also surfaces as HTTP 200 with content='' from api/v1/generate.py:79-87.

In a bulk job every row 'succeeds' with empty generated_content, errors stays empty, and final_status=SUCCEEDED — a 1000-row job reported fully successful with zero content produced.

title: Migration 001 cannot run on PostgreSQL: partitioned tables declare PK(id) without the partition key, and child FKs reference content_pieces(id) alone
root_cause: PostgreSQL requires every PK/unique constraint on a partitioned table to include all partition-key columns. content_pieces is PARTITION BY HASH(workspace_id) with PRIMARY KEY(id); audit_logs (~line 477), experiment_assignments (~662), experiment_exposures (~706) and performance_events (~757) have the same defect. Child FKs (content_versions.content_piece_id line 306, review_annotations line 336, performance_events line 758) reference only content_pieces.id, which is illegal against a partitioned table. Tests pass only because they run on SQLite, where postgresql_partition_by is ignored.
suggested_fix: Make PKs composite — PrimaryKeyConstraint('id','workspace_id') for content_pieces, ('id',<partition_col>) for RANGE tables — and change child FKs to composite references with a matching workspace_id column on children, or drop declarative partitioning. Add a CI job running alembic upgrade head against a real PostgreSQL 16 container.
failure_scenario: Fresh deployment: alembic upgrade head on PostgreSQL 16 aborts at CREATE TABLE content_pieces with 'insufficient columns in the primary key definition for partitioned table'; no schema is created. Even with the PK fixed, content_versions creation fails with 'no unique constraint matching given keys for referenced table content_pieces'.

title: Paused bulk job never observes resume/cancel: _wait_for_resume loops forever on a stale identity-map instance and wedges the worker
root_cause: The session factory uses expire_on_commit=False (db/session.py:101). BulkJobService.get_job/get_job_unscoped (services/bulk_job_service.py:48-67) issue plain selects without populate_existing, so a re-SELECT of an already-loaded BulkJob returns the cached object without refreshing attributes. Inside _wait_for_resume nothing ever commits/refreshes/expires, so fresh.status stays PAUSED forever after the API sets RUNNING/CANCELLED in the DB. Pause is only noticed by accident because increment_progress calls db.refresh. The standalone worker processes messages sequentially, so one wedged job blocks all further jobs.
suggested_fix: Add .execution_options(populate_existing=True) to get_job/get_job_unscoped selects, or db.refresh()/expire the instance on every poll in _wait_for_resume and the pause/cancel gate; add a max pause duration after which the job is failed/cancelled.
failure_scenario: Pause a running job (worker enters _wait_for_resume), then resume or cancel via the API: DB row becomes RUNNING/CANCELLED but every poll returns the cached PAUSED object. The job never resumes, that worker replica processes no further jobs, and SIGTERM cannot break the loop. The PAUSED job is also never reaped (reaper targets RUNNING/PENDING only).
verification_notes: cd pulse-api && .venv/bin/pytest tests -q -> 107 passed (exit 0); ruff/mypy clean. get_job/get_job_unscoped now use populate_existing=True. Regression test: test_get_job_observes_external_status_change (tests/test_worker_pipeline.py).

title: $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) never expands because the variable comes from envFrom; all three Python services crash-loop
root_cause: Kubernetes $(VAR) expansion in env values only resolves variables defined earlier in the same container's env list; variables injected via envFrom secretRef/configMapRef are not part of the expansion map. POSTGRES_PASSWORD exists only in pulse-secrets via envFrom, so the reference is left verbatim. Identical pattern in k8s/pulse-worker.yaml:24-26 and k8s/pulse-scheduler.yaml:26-28. The manifest comment incorrectly claims it expands.
suggested_fix: Define POSTGRES_PASSWORD explicitly in the env list via valueFrom.secretKeyRef before DATABASE_URL in each of the three manifests, or store the full DATABASE_URL as a Secret key and consume it directly.
failure_scenario: kubectl apply -f k8s/ as-is -> DATABASE_URL contains the literal '$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)' -> asyncpg authentication failure -> pulse-api, pulse-worker and pulse-scheduler all CrashLoopBackOff; the whole stack is dead.

title: Bulk-job input/output files live in container-local /tmp with no shared volume; jobs always fail in the multi-container deployment
root_cause: The API writes uploads to its own container's tempfile.gettempdir()/pulse_bulk_uploads (line 40, 88-89); the worker checks Path(input_path).exists() on its own filesystem (worker/tasks.py:89-94) and writes outputs to its own /tmp. docker-compose.yml defines no volumes for pulse-api/pulse-worker and k8s has no shared PVC; the API also runs 2 replicas. The comment 'must match worker.tasks' matches only the path string, not the filesystem. The download endpoint (bulk_jobs.py:240) likewise never sees the worker's output file.
suggested_fix: Store input/output blobs in the already-provisioned S3/MinIO storage (STORAGE_* settings exist) and keep URIs in input_file/output_file, or mount a shared ReadWriteMany volume at the same path in API and worker containers; key objects by job id.
failure_scenario: Compose/k8s with Redis up: POST /bulk-jobs succeeds, the standalone worker consumes the message, Path(input_file).exists() is False in the worker container -> every job FAILED with 'Input file missing'. Even if processing succeeded, GET /bulk-jobs/{id}/download 404s permanently. Only the Redis-down in-process fallback on a single API instance works.

NOTE: k8s PVCs need a ReadWriteMany-capable StorageClass (documented in manifest); live compose/k8s run pending Docker host.

title: Non-atomic PENDING->RUNNING check allows duplicate processing of the same job
root_cause: The at-least-once guard reads job.status (get_job_unscoped) and only later commits RUNNING via svc.update_status; there is no row lock or conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending'. Duplicate stream messages are routine: the reaper re-enqueues PENDING jobs older than 10 min even when the original message is still queued, and scheduler + worker-startup reapers can run concurrently. Two workers blocked on XREADGROUP can receive the two copies simultaneously. Related: #27 (progress read-modify-write race).
suggested_fix: Claim atomically: UPDATE bulk_jobs SET status='running', updated_at=now() WHERE id=:id AND status='pending' RETURNING id (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and proceed only if a row was claimed; apply the same conditional transition in mark_job_failed/reaper.
failure_scenario: Job sits in the stream >10 min (worker busy) -> reaper re-enqueues a second copy -> workers A and B each consume one copy, both read PENDING, both set RUNNING, both generate every row (double LLM spend), both increment progress via read-modify-write (lost updates), both overwrite <job_id>.csv.
verification_notes: 107 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. New BulkJobService.claim_pending_job: conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' RETURNING id; tasks.py uses it. Regression tests: test_claim_pending_job_is_atomic, test_process_bulk_job_outcomes_for_non_pending_jobs.

title: XAUTOCLAIM min-idle (60s) is shorter than job runtime: a second worker claims and ACKs a message another worker is still processing, destroying crash recovery
root_cause: Messages are acked only after the whole job finishes and nothing extends PEL idle time during processing. DEFAULT_MIN_IDLE_MS=60_000 (line 37) while multi-row LLM jobs run for minutes. With 2 worker replicas, worker B's _recover_pending XAUTOCLAIMs worker A's in-flight message; tasks.py sees status RUNNING and returns normally (skip path), then handle_message acks it (line 231). The message leaves the PEL while A is still working.
suggested_fix: Make the visibility timeout exceed worst-case job duration or implement heartbeat/claim-extension (periodic XCLAIM JUSTID to reset idle while processing); never ack a message whose job is RUNNING unless this consumer owns it — ack only after verifying the job reached a terminal state owned by this delivery.
failure_scenario: Worker A processes a 5-minute job; after 60s worker B claims the message, sees RUNNING, acks it. A is then OOM-killed mid-job: no pending message remains, so no retry ever happens; the job sits RUNNING until the reaper marks it FAILED 10 minutes later. Work is lost and never reprocessed.
verification_notes: 107 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. process_bulk_job returns processed/terminal/active; handle_message never acks 'active' outcomes; PEL heartbeat (_extend_claim_loop + RedisClient.extend_claim XCLAIM JUSTID) keeps in-flight messages from being stolen. Regression test: test_worker_does_not_ack_job_active_elsewhere.

title: Results endpoint crashes (ValueError) when conversions exceed unique visitors — negative contingency cells and asin domain error
root_cause: compute_results (core/experiment/results.py:49-57) counts every conversion EVENT while the denominator is deduplicated visitors, and ingestion accepts events without visitor_hash, so conversions > total is reachable. chi_squared_test guards only n==0 and denominator==0: b=total-conversions<0 can make the denominator negative -> chi2<0 -> math.sqrt(chi2/2) ValueError; independently p1=conversions/visitors>1 feeds math.asin(math.sqrt(p1)) (lines 80-82) -> math domain error. Both propagate as unhandled 500 from GET /experiments/{id}/results. Even without a crash, negative cells produce meaningless p-values.
suggested_fix: Validate 0 <= conversions <= total for both groups and return the 'Invalid sample sizes' result otherwise; clamp proportions to [0,1] for Cohen's h; fix the counting model (#43) and validate conversion/visitor consistency at ingestion.
failure_scenario: Any member posts 10 conversion events with visitor_hash=null plus 1 impression with visitor_hash='v1' to a running experiment (server-side conversion tracking without visitor IDs is normal). GET /experiments/{id}/results -> asin(sqrt(10)) ValueError -> 500; results and promote-winner permanently unusable for that experiment. Also reachable cross-workspace via #12.
verification_notes: 107 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. chi_squared_test and bayesian_analysis reject conversions>visitors with 'Invalid sample sizes'; Cohen's h proportions clamped to [0,1]. Regression test: test_chi_squared_rejects_conversions_exceeding_visitors (tests/test_experiments.py). Root counting-model fix tracked separately as #43.

title: Impersonation grants any self-registered owner full access to ANY workspace
root_cause: POST /auth/impersonate only checks that the caller's token role is 'owner' and that the target workspace row exists; it never verifies membership/administration of the target. get_current_user validates only user existence/is_active, not that the token's workspace_id matches the user's DB workspace, so the minted token is accepted everywhere. Registration is open, so anyone can become an 'owner'. The audit row is written to the caller's workspace only — the victim workspace has no record. (Acknowledged as a TODO in the docstring/CLAUDE.md, but it is a live cross-tenant authz bypass, distinct from the documented RLS gap.)
suggested_fix: Require an explicit membership/admin record linking the user to the target workspace (or restrict impersonation to a platform super-admin role); write the audit event into the target workspace as well; optionally re-check workspace membership in get_current_user.
failure_scenario: Attacker registers workspace A (becomes OWNER), obtains victim workspace B's UUID, POSTs /auth/impersonate {target_workspace_id: B} -> receives a valid owner-scoped JWT for B and can read/modify/delete all of B's content, experiments, users and webhooks.
verification_notes: 110 tests pass (exit 0), ruff/mypy clean. Impersonation now requires the caller's DB user row to belong to the target workspace (403 otherwise) until cross-workspace membership exists. Regression test: test_impersonate_foreign_workspace_forbidden. Existing same-workspace impersonate tests still pass.

title: Performance-event ingestion has no workspace/ownership check (cross-workspace write IDOR)
root_cause: ingest_performance_event and ingest_performance_events_batch pass client-supplied experiment_id/variant_id straight to ExperimentService.ingest_event/ingest_events_batch (services/experiment_service.py:266-327), which never loads the experiment, never filters by workspace_id, never checks the variant belongs to the experiment, and never checks experiment status. This is a missing service-layer tenant filter (the current isolation boundary). experiment_id is semi-public (embedded in tracking URLs, core/experiment/tracking.py). Unknown UUIDs surface as unhandled FK IntegrityErrors (500, whole batch rolled back).
suggested_fix: Pass current_user.workspace_id into both ingest methods; load the experiment scoped to the workspace (404 otherwise); verify variant.experiment_id == experiment_id and experiment status before inserting; catch IntegrityError and return 400/404 instead of 500.
failure_scenario: An authenticated user in workspace A who learns workspace B's experiment_id (from a published tracking URL) POSTs /performance-events/batch with thousands of fake conversion events, corrupting B's experiment results and winner recommendation; a leaked variant UUID lets the attacker fabricate conversions and flip the promoted winner. Random UUIDs yield unhandled 500s.
verification_notes: 110 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. ingest_event/ingest_events_batch take workspace_id; _validate_event_target checks experiment ownership (404) and variant<->experiment consistency (400); IntegrityError -> 400; events now store workspace_id. Regression tests: test_ingest_rejects_foreign_workspace_experiment, test_ingest_rejects_mismatched_variant.

title: Unsanitized user input interpolated into the system prompt (prompt injection)
root_cause: content_type and target_market are unconstrained free-text strings (generation/models.py) and cultural_overrides is an arbitrary dict; persuasion_style is popped from user-controlled overrides with no enum validation (cultural/engine.py). All are inserted via str.format into _DEFAULT_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE, so attacker-chosen text becomes part of the system instruction block. The same values flow in from bulk-job CSV columns (worker/tasks.py).
suggested_fix: Validate content_type against an allowlist and target_market against a locale pattern in GenerationRequest; restrict persuasion_style to the known enum and clamp/validate override keys; reject or escape newlines/control text in values destined for the system template.
failure_scenario: POST /generate with content_type='blog_post\n\nIgnore all cultural guidelines above...' (or crafted cultural_overrides) -> injected text rendered inside the system prompt sent to the LLM. Also deliverable via a crafted CSV content_type column in bulk jobs.
verification_notes: 116 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. GenerationRequest validators restrict content_type/target_market to safe charsets; cultural adapt accepts only known dimension keys and the 4 supported persuasion styles. Regression tests: test_generation_request_rejects_prompt_injection, test_cultural_overrides_are_sanitized.

title: Composed system prompt is concatenated into a single user message, defeating instruction hierarchy
root_cause: The orchestrator flattens system+user into full_prompt and every adapter sends it as one user-role message (openai.py:76, anthropic.py:77, ollama.py:68). PromptComposer.compose_messages() exists but is never used. The 'system' cultural/brand guidelines carry no system-role authority and are trivially overridden by user instructions in the same message.
suggested_fix: Pass system and user prompts separately through the provider interface; use OpenAI chat 'system' role and Anthropic's top-level 'system' parameter; keep user-supplied instructions strictly in the user message.
failure_scenario: Any /generate request: cultural guidelines and user instructions arrive as one user message; 'Disregard the guidelines above' overrides them with no privilege boundary, and the recorded system/user split is not what the model receives.
verification_notes: 116 tests pass. LLMProvider.generate gains system kwarg; OpenAI uses system-role message, Anthropic top-level system param, Ollama system field; orchestrator sends composed system/user separately. Regression test: test_system_prompt_sent_separately.

title: Client-caused 4xx errors trip the global circuit breaker for all tenants
root_cause: Providers return finish_reason='error' for any httpx.HTTPStatusError, including 400 (invalid user llm_params/model), 401 and 429. The orchestrator records every such error as a provider failure, and the FallbackRouter is a process-global singleton shared by all workspaces. No distinction between caller errors and provider health.
suggested_fix: Only count 5xx/network/timeout errors toward the circuit breaker; propagate 4xx as request errors (do not record_failure). Consider per-provider or per-tenant breaker state instead of one global router.
failure_scenario: Three users send llm_params={'temperature': 5} -> OpenAI 400 x3 -> failure_threshold=3 -> circuit OPEN for 60s -> every other tenant's generation is rerouted even though the primary is healthy.
verification_notes: 116 tests pass. Orchestrator records breaker failures only for 5xx/network errors (4xx propagated as GenerationError without record_failure). Regression test: test_client_error_does_not_trip_breaker.

title: record_failure is provider-agnostic: secondary failures keep resetting the primary recovery timer
root_cause: _last_failure_time is updated on every failure regardless of which provider produced it or the current state. While OPEN, all traffic goes to the secondary; each secondary failure refreshes _last_failure_time, so the OPEN->HALF_OPEN condition can never become true while the secondary keeps failing. The router never tracks which provider a routed request used.
suggested_fix: Track the provider returned by route_request and only update _last_failure_time for primary failures; or timestamp the OPEN transition itself and ignore failures recorded while OPEN.
failure_scenario: Primary hits a transient outage -> circuit OPEN. Secondary is quota-exhausted (429 every call). Every secondary failure resets the timer, so even after the primary recovers it is never re-probed: all traffic stays pinned to the failing secondary indefinitely.
verification_notes: 116 tests pass. record_failure ignores failures while OPEN (timer runs from open moment); provider-aware recording via optional provider arg. Regression test: test_secondary_failures_do_not_extend_recovery_timer.

title: HALF_OPEN admits unlimited concurrent probes to the primary
root_cause: After recovery_timeout elapses, route_request transitions to HALF_OPEN and returns primary for every subsequent request until a failure is recorded. No probe cap or in-flight tracking, so a burst of concurrent requests all hit a possibly-still-dead primary simultaneously; with 60s provider timeouts each hangs for the full timeout before the first failure re-opens the circuit.
suggested_fix: Limit HALF_OPEN to a fixed number of in-flight probe requests; route all other requests to the secondary until the probes conclude. Track in-flight probe count in route_request/record_success/record_failure.
failure_scenario: Primary down; 60s pass; 50 concurrent /generate requests arrive while primary is still slow-failing. All 50 are routed to the dead primary and hang ~60s each instead of using the secondary.
verification_notes: 116 tests pass. HALF_OPEN admits at most success_threshold concurrent probes; excess traffic stays on secondary; probe count reset on transition. Regression test: test_half_open_limits_concurrent_probes.

title: Language-only fallback selects the first registered region variant, producing wrong-market dimensions
root_cause: _get_base_dimensions iterates self._dimensions in insertion order and returns the first code matching '{lang}-'. No region-aware or configured fallback: any unknown region variant silently inherits whichever variant happens to be first in the dict. The DB fallback_code chain (load_market_profile_with_fallback) is never used by the orchestrator.
suggested_fix: Use an explicit language-level default map (or the market profile's fallback_code chain) instead of dict-order matching; prefer load_market_profile_with_fallback in the generation path.
failure_scenario: target_market='zh-TW'/'zh-HK' -> falls back to zh-CN dimensions; 'pt-PT' -> pt-BR; 'en-AU'/'en-CA' -> en-US; 'ar-EG' -> ar-SA. Content generated with culturally wrong settings, silently; result also depends on registration order.
verification_notes: 119 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. Explicit _LANGUAGE_FALLBACK map replaces dict-order matching. Regression test: test_language_fallback_is_explicit_not_dict_order.

title: Brand voice loading (pipeline step 2) is dead code: brand_voice_id is silently ignored
root_cause: brand_voice_data is initialized to {} at line 97 and never assigned anywhere — no DB query for brand_voice_id exists despite the docstring claiming step 2 loads it. The 'if brand_voice_data:' branch (line 116) can never execute, so brand_voice_section is always empty.
suggested_fix: Implement the brand voice lookup (query BrandVoice by request.brand_voice_id within the session, build tone_profile section) or remove the dead branch and document brand_voice_id as unsupported; add a test asserting the brand voice section appears when brand_voice_id is provided.
failure_scenario: Client creates a brand voice and sends brand_voice_id in /generate or bulk config: the prompt contains no brand voice guidance and the response echoes brand_voice_id as if applied — tone consistency is a silent no-op.
verification_notes: 119 tests pass. Orchestrator now loads BrandVoice workspace-scoped when brand_voice_id + workspace_id provided; routers/worker pass workspace_id. Regression test: test_brand_voice_and_db_market_profile_are_applied (asserts tone description reaches system prompt).

title: DB market-profile enrichment never runs: production callers pass no db_session_factory
root_cause: The orchestrator only loads DB market profiles when db_session_factory is set, but the production constructor (api/v1/generate.py:59, also used by worker/tasks.py) calls GenerationOrchestrator(fallback_router=...) without it. DB-configured cultural_dimensions and the fallback_code chain are always ignored; generation always uses hardcoded built-in defaults.
suggested_fix: Pass the async session factory when constructing the orchestrator in get_orchestrator() (and use load_market_profile_with_fallback so fallback_code is honored), or inject per-request sessions; add a test covering DB-profile-driven dimensions.
failure_scenario: Admin seeds market_profiles with custom cultural_dimensions for 'de-DE' (formality 0.9). POST /generate target_market='de-DE' -> orchestrator skips the DB (factory is None) and uses built-in defaults (0.7); the configured profile has no effect, silently.
verification_notes: 119 tests pass. get_orchestrator wires get_session_factory(); orchestrator uses load_market_profile_with_fallback (DB fallback_code chain honored). Same regression test asserts DB cultural_dimensions override built-ins.

title: bulk_job_status enum in migration omits 'paused' which the ORM model and pause() write
root_cause: models/bulk_job.py BulkJobStatus defines PAUSED='paused' and BulkJobService.pause() sets it, but migration 001 creates the native enum with only pending/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled and migration 002 never adds the value. On PostgreSQL the UPDATE fails; on SQLite (tests) the enum is a VARCHAR so the drift is invisible. Frontend type also omits it (#67).
suggested_fix: Add 'paused' to the enum in 001 (or a new migration with ALTER TYPE bulk_job_status ADD VALUE 'paused'), and add a model-vs-migration enum consistency test.
failure_scenario: On PostgreSQL, POST /bulk-jobs/{id}/pause on a RUNNING job raises asyncpg InvalidTextRepresentationError -> HTTP 500; resume() is unreachable and the worker's PAUSED gate is dead code.
verification_notes: 119 tests pass. Migration 001 bulk_job_status enum now includes 'paused' (matches ORM). Drift-guard test: test_migration_enum_and_jsonb_match_models.

title: All JSONB model columns are created as plain JSON by the migration (schema drift)
root_cause: Every ORM model declares JSONB (workspace.settings, content.metadata, brand_voices, glossary, bulk_jobs.errors, audit_logs.details, experiment configuration, prompt variables, performance/exposure metadata, generation_cache.metadata — ~18 columns), but migration 001 uses sa.JSON for all of them. On PostgreSQL sa.JSON renders the json type, not jsonb.
suggested_fix: Use sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.JSONB in the migration for these columns (or a follow-up ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE jsonb migration) so the database matches Base.metadata; verify with alembic check.
failure_scenario: alembic check/autogenerate permanently reports ~18 type mismatches and generates spurious migrations; any future JSONB operator (metadata @>, GIN index) fails at runtime with 'operator does not exist: json @> json'.
verification_notes: 119 tests pass. All 19 sa.JSON columns in migration 001 replaced with postgresql.JSONB to match ORM models. Same drift-guard test asserts no sa.JSON remains.

title: performance_events has RLS enabled nowhere and no policy, so tenant telemetry stays unprotected even after RLS becomes binding
root_cause: workspace_scoped_tables lists 16 tables but omits performance_events, which holds per-tenant business metrics linked via experiment_id/content_piece_id. Migration 002 FORCEs RLS on the same list, so performance_events never gets ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY nor a policy.
suggested_fix: Enable RLS on performance_events and add a parent-style policy (EXISTS over experiments/content_pieces matching pulse.workspace_id), or add a workspace_id column with a direct policy; include it in 002's FORCE list.
failure_scenario: After the non-owner role rollout, a session scoped to workspace A can SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE performance_events rows belonging to workspace B's experiments because no policy restricts the table while all sibling tables are restricted.
verification_notes: 123 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. performance_events added to 001 RLS enable+direct policy lists, downgrade policy list, and 002 FORCE list (workspace_id column added in #3, populated in #12). Drift-guard test: test_migration_rls_and_default_partitions_cover_telemetry.

title: Fixed partition windows with no DEFAULT partition and no partition-maintenance job: inserts start failing when windows expire
root_cause: audit_logs/experiment_assignments get 24 monthly partitions (Jan 2026–Dec 2027); experiment_exposures/performance_events get 52 weekly partitions ending 2027-01-04. No DEFAULT partition is created and nothing in the codebase creates future partitions (worker/maintenance.py only reaps bulk jobs). RANGE partitioned tables reject rows outside all partitions.
suggested_fix: Add a DEFAULT partition as a safety net plus a scheduled job that creates upcoming monthly/weekly partitions ahead of time (or pg_partman). Also handle backdated rows (created_at < 2026-01-01) which fail today.
failure_scenario: From 2027-01-04 (~6 weeks after this audit), every INSERT into performance_events/experiment_exposures fails with 'no partition of relation found for row', breaking event ingestion; from 2028-01-01 audit_logs inserts fail, breaking auth flows that write AuditLog rows.
verification_notes: 123 tests pass. DEFAULT partitions added for all 4 RANGE-partitioned tables (upgrade + downgrade): out-of-window/backdated rows no longer fail INSERTs. Same drift-guard test. Future-window maintenance job still recommended (documented in migration comment).

title: Admin-session fallback to DATABASE_URL silently breaks login/registration once RLS is enforced as migration 002 intends
root_cause: get_admin_session_factory falls back to s.database_url when database_admin_url is empty (the docker-compose default). Migration 002 FORCEs RLS and documents switching DATABASE_URL to the non-owner pulse_api role; pre-auth login/registration queries run without any pulse.workspace_id setting, so the users policy denies all rows. Even pointing DATABASE_ADMIN_URL at the table owner is insufficient because FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY binds the owner too — only a superuser/BYPASSRLS role bypasses it. The same trap empties worker/scheduler unscoped queries under the scoped role.
suggested_fix: Fail fast at startup when RLS is enforced and database_admin_url is unset or equals database_url; document that the admin role needs BYPASSRLS; give worker/scheduler a trusted role or set workspace context per job.
failure_scenario: Operator follows 002's rollout, leaves DATABASE_ADMIN_URL empty (compose default). POST /auth/login finds zero users for valid credentials (RLS deny-by-default) -> universal 401; registration INSERT rejected by WITH CHECK; the bulk-job reaper finds zero stale jobs.
verification_notes: 123 tests pass. New PULSE_RLS_ENFORCED setting (default false); get_admin_session_factory raises RuntimeError when enforced and DATABASE_ADMIN_URL unset/equal to DATABASE_URL. .env.example documents it. Regression test: test_admin_factory_requires_distinct_url_when_rls_enforced.

title: Job state transitions are check-then-act without row locking; worker's final commit overwrites CANCELLED with SUCCEEDED
root_cause: cancel()/pause()/resume()/update_status() read the job, validate status in Python, and commit without SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status = <expected>. The worker (worker/tasks.py:153-165) likewise decides final_status from a read and then unconditionally sets job.status, so a cancel committed between the worker's last status read and its final commit is silently overwritten. Related: #8, #42.
suggested_fix: Use atomic conditional updates (UPDATE bulk_jobs SET status=:new WHERE id=:id AND status IN (:allowed) RETURNING *) or SELECT FOR UPDATE inside the transition, and make the worker's final write conditional on status not being CANCELLED.
failure_scenario: User cancels a job while the worker is writing the output CSV. Worker commits status=SUCCEEDED over CANCELLED; the UI shows the cancelled job as succeeded and its output is downloadable. Two concurrent pause/cancel requests can also both pass their status checks.
verification_notes: 123 tests pass. pause/resume/cancel use atomic conditional UPDATE (_transition_status with allowed-status WHERE); worker final write conditional on RUNNING/PAUSED so CANCELLED/reaped states are never overwritten. Regression test: test_state_transitions_are_conditional.

title: increment_progress is a read-modify-write race; concurrent workers lose progress updates
root_cause: progress is computed in Python ((job.progress or 0) + count) and written back, not via an atomic SQL increment. Combined with the non-atomic job claim (#8) and XAUTOCLAIM redelivery (#9), two workers processing the same job interleave increments and lose updates.
suggested_fix: Increment atomically: UPDATE bulk_jobs SET progress = progress + :count, updated_at=now() WHERE id=:id.
failure_scenario: Duplicate delivery (see #8/#9): two workers both generate rows and call increment_progress concurrently; final progress < total, job appears stuck below 100% even after completion.
verification_notes: 123 tests pass. increment_progress now atomic SQL UPDATE progress = coalesce(progress,0) + count. Regression test: test_increment_progress_accumulates_atomically.

title: promote_winner mutates the JSONB configuration dict in place; SQLAlchemy never persists the winner info
root_cause: config = experiment.configuration or {} returns the same dict object already loaded; it is mutated and reassigned. Without MutableDict tracking, attribute history compares the new value against the committed value — the same mutated object — finds no change, and the UPDATE emitted for status/ended_at/updated_at does not include the configuration column. Only when configuration was None or {} does a fresh dict get assigned and persist.
suggested_fix: Assign a copy: config = dict(experiment.configuration or {}); config[...] = ...; experiment.configuration = config — or wrap the column type with MutableDict.as_mutable(JSONB).
failure_scenario: Experiment with configuration={'randomisation_unit':'visitor'} is RUNNING; POST /experiments/{id}/promote-winner returns 200 with winner info, but the configuration row is unchanged — promoted_winner_id/name silently lost.
verification_notes: 129 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. promote_winner assigns dict(experiment.configuration or {}) so SQLAlchemy detects the change. Regression test: test_promote_winner_persists_configuration (re-reads row after rollback).

title: Unbounded event batch ingestion and full-table event load in results (OOM vector)
root_cause: get_results selects every PerformanceEvent for an experiment with no limit/time window — a table designed as very high-volume and weekly-partitioned — into a Python list, then builds a second list of dicts. Additionally PerformanceEventBatchCreate.events has no max_length (api/schemas/experiment.py:182-184) and ingest_events_batch builds one ORM object per event in a single transaction (api/v1/experiments.py:390-412). Amplifiable cross-workspace via #12.
suggested_fix: Aggregate in SQL (GROUP BY variant_id, metric_type with COUNT/COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id)/SUM(value)) and feed only aggregates to compute_results; cap batch size (e.g. 1000 events, 422 beyond) and insert in chunks.
failure_scenario: Client POSTs /performance-events/batch with 1M events -> multi-GB transaction; afterwards every GET /experiments/{id}/results materializes all rows in RAM (API pod limit 1Gi in k8s) -> event-loop stall, OOM kill of the API pod.
verification_notes: 129 tests pass. get_results aggregates in SQL (GROUP BY variant/metric/visitor with counts) instead of loading all ORM events; compute_results accepts count; batch schema capped at 1000 events (422 beyond). Regression test: test_event_batch_rejects_oversized_payload; existing results tests pass through the aggregation path.

title: Logout does not clear the TanStack Query cache — cross-workspace data bleed on next login
root_cause: handleLogout removes the token and does an SPA navigate('/login') without queryClient.clear(). All query keys (['me'], ['content'], ['dashboard-totals'], ['bulk-jobs'], ['experiments'], ...) are workspace-agnostic and stay cached for the default 5-minute gcTime. The 401 interceptor path does a full page reload (clearing the cache), but the normal logout path does not.
suggested_fix: Call queryClient.clear() in handleLogout before navigating, and/or scope query keys by workspace_id from the token. Also clear on login when the identity changes.
failure_scenario: User A (workspace X) logs out; user B (workspace Y) signs in within 5 minutes in the same tab. Dashboard immediately renders workspace X's cached totals and content titles, and Layout shows A's email, until refetch resolves. If B's refetch fails, workspace X's data remains displayed indefinitely.
verification_notes: Frontend typecheck/lint/build exit 0. handleLogout calls queryClient.clear() before navigating (Layout.tsx).

title: JWT persisted in localStorage is readable by any XSS
root_cause: The access token is stored under 'pulse_token' in localStorage (written in Login.tsx) and attached by the request interceptor. localStorage is accessible to any script running in the origin; there is no CSP (#68) and no httpOnly-cookie alternative, so a single XSS or compromised dependency exfiltrates a token valid until exp (server-side revocation only on explicit logout).
suggested_fix: Prefer an httpOnly SameSite cookie session (or keep the access token in memory with a refresh cookie). At minimum add a strict CSP and shorten token TTL.
failure_scenario: An XSS payload executes localStorage.getItem('pulse_token') and sends the JWT to an attacker, who can call /api/v1/* as the victim until the token expires — logout-everywhere is never triggered.
verification_notes: httpOnly-cookie session migration is an architectural change (backend cookie auth + CSRF protection + refresh flow) beyond a minimal scoped fix. Mitigations landed this round: ephemeral dev signing keys (#53), SPA security headers (#68), existing 30-min token TTL and server-side revocation. Recommend planning the cookie migration as a dedicated task.

title: nginx default client_max_body_size (1 MiB) rejects bulk CSV uploads the backend accepts (5 MiB); k8s ingress has the same cap
root_cause: No client_max_body_size is set in the server or /api/ location, so nginx applies its 1m default. POST /bulk-jobs allows up to MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 5 MiB (api/v1/bulk_jobs.py:37). The k8s ingress also has no nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size annotation (k8s/ingress.yaml), so the same 1m cap applies there.
suggested_fix: Add client_max_body_size 6m; to the server block (or /api/ location) and set nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: "6m" on the ingress to match.
failure_scenario: In compose/k8s a user uploads a 2 MiB CSV (under the backend's 5 MiB limit): nginx/ingress returns 413 before the request reaches pulse-api; the UI shows a generic 413 error and no job is created.
verification_notes: nginx server block sets client_max_body_size 6m; ingress gets proxy-body-size: 6m annotation. Matches API's 5 MiB limit.

title: Default 60s proxy_read_timeout truncates long synchronous /generate requests
root_cause: The /api/ proxy sets no proxy_read_timeout/proxy_send_timeout, so nginx's 60s default applies. POST /generate is fully synchronous and LLM adapters allow 60s (OpenAI/Anthropic) to 120s (Ollama) per call plus circuit-breaker fallback — total backend latency can legitimately exceed 60s. The axios client sets no timeout either.
suggested_fix: Set proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s; on the /api/ location (or a dedicated /api/v1/generate location), matching worst-case provider timeout + fallback.
failure_scenario: An Ollama-backed generation takes 90s. At 60s nginx returns 504; the UI shows 'Generation failed' while the backend keeps running. The user retries, producing duplicate content and double LLM spend.
verification_notes: nginx /api/ location sets proxy_read_timeout/proxy_send_timeout 300s (covers 120s Ollama + fallback).

title: crypto.randomUUID() crashes the Experiments page on non-secure (HTTP) origins
root_cause: crypto.randomUUID is only available in secure contexts (HTTPS or localhost). The shipped deployment topologies serve plain HTTP: docker-compose maps 5173:80 and k8s/ingress.yaml exposes http://pulse.local with no TLS (#39). newVariantDraft is called in the useState initializer, so the TypeError fires during first render.
suggested_fix: Use a fallback key generator, e.g. crypto.randomUUID?.() ?? `v-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`, or a module-level counter.
failure_scenario: User opens http://pulse.local/experiments (k8s) or http://<server-ip>:5173/experiments (compose on a remote host): crypto.randomUUID is undefined -> TypeError in the state initializer -> whole page replaced by the ErrorBoundary screen; experiments cannot be viewed or created.
verification_notes: Frontend checks exit 0. newVariantDraft uses crypto.randomUUID?.() with Date.now/Math.random fallback for non-secure contexts.

title: Bulk job list never refreshes while jobs run asynchronously — progress appears frozen
root_cause: The ['bulk-jobs'] query has no refetchInterval, and main.tsx disables refetchOnWindowFocus globally. Jobs are processed asynchronously by pulse-worker after creation, but the only refetch triggers are component remount or the create mutation's own invalidate.
suggested_fix: Add refetchInterval: (query) => query.state.data?.some(j => j.status === 'pending' || j.status === 'running') ? 3000 : false.
failure_scenario: User uploads a 100-row CSV and stays on the page: the row shows 'pending 0/100' indefinitely even after the worker finishes; the Download CSV button never appears until the user navigates away and back.
verification_notes: Frontend checks exit 0. ['bulk-jobs'] query polls every 3s while any job is pending/running (TanStack v5 refetchInterval callback).

title: downloadResults has no error handling — failed downloads are silent unhandled rejections
root_cause: downloadResults is an async onClick handler with no try/catch and no mutation error state. Any non-2xx (e.g. 404 when the worker's temp output was cleaned up, or 401) rejects unhandled. Additionally URL.revokeObjectURL is called synchronously right after anchor.click(), which can race the download start in some browsers (notably Firefox).
suggested_fix: Wrap in try/catch and surface the failure via setError(apiErrorMessage(...)); revoke the object URL in setTimeout(..., 0) or after the load event.
failure_scenario: A job shows output_file set but the file was removed. Clicking 'Download CSV' produces a 404; the promise rejects unhandled (console-only), no error is shown, and the button appears to do nothing.
verification_notes: Frontend checks exit 0. downloadResults wrapped in try/catch surfacing apiErrorMessage; revokeObjectURL deferred via setTimeout.

title: List pages silently truncate at the backend's default 20 rows — no pagination, total discarded
root_cause: GET /content defaults to limit=20 (max 100) and returns {items, total}, but fetchContent keeps only items and the page renders no pager or 'showing X of Y' indicator. The identical pattern exists in BulkJobs.tsx:6-10 and Experiments.tsx:12-16.
suggested_fix: Read total from the ListResponse and add offset-based pagination (or useInfiniteQuery), requesting explicit limit/offset params.
failure_scenario: A workspace has 50 content pieces: the Content page shows only the first 20 with no indication more exist; pieces 21-50 are unreachable through the UI (same for bulk jobs and experiments beyond 20).
verification_notes: Frontend checks exit 0. ContentList/BulkJobs/Experiments fetch explicit limit/offset, keep total, render Showing X-Y of N + Previous/Next pager; query keys offset-scoped, invalidation prefix-matches.

title: Example Secret is incompatible with the shipped ConfigMap: applying k8s/ as-is makes the API refuse to start
root_cause: secrets.example.yaml ships PULSE_SECRET_KEY='change-me-in-production' and WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET='whsec_change_me', while k8s/configmap.yaml sets PULSE_ENV='production'. create_app() raises RuntimeError in production when either secret equals its default. The file header claims it is 'for local/dev clusters' but nothing in the manifests runs the app in development mode.
suggested_fix: Provide a dev overlay with PULSE_ENV=development, or make the example values obviously non-default placeholders with a clear README step; at minimum document that applying secrets.example.yaml unchanged guarantees CrashLoopBackOff.
failure_scenario: Operator copies secrets.example.yaml to secrets.yaml and applies k8s/*.yaml without editing values -> create_app() raises 'Refusing to start in production with default secrets' -> pulse-api CrashLoopBackOff.
verification_notes: secrets.example.yaml header now documents required copy/replace/apply steps and that unchanged values intentionally CrashLoopBackOff via the production guard (fail-closed kept). REDIS_PASSWORD key added.

title: Ingress has no TLS section; login credentials and JWTs travel in plaintext
root_cause: spec contains only rules, no tls block and no cert-manager/ssl-redirect annotations. The ingress routes /api (auth login/register, bearer tokens) and the SPA over plain HTTP. Also enables #34 (secure-context APIs unavailable).
suggested_fix: Add a spec.tls entry with a certificate (cert-manager annotation or pre-provisioned secret) and an nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect annotation.
failure_scenario: Deploy as-is -> user logs in at http://pulse.local -> password and access_token sent unencrypted, capturable by any on-path observer; tokens replayable for their full lifetime.
verification_notes: Requires a certificate-provisioning decision (cert-manager issuer vs pre-provisioned secret) that belongs to the operator. Added a ready-to-enable commented tls block + cert-manager/ssl-redirect annotation template in k8s/ingress.yaml; enabling without a valid cert would serve the controller's default self-signed cert. Related: #34 fallback makes the UI work over HTTP meanwhile.

title: Redis runs as an ephemeral, unauthenticated Deployment; a pod restart wipes token-revocation markers and bulk-job stream state
root_cause: Redis is a Deployment with no volume/PVC and no requirepass/AUTH, and there are no NetworkPolicy manifests. auth/revocation.py stores the jti blocklist and logout-everywhere cutoffs only in this Redis, and the bulk-job stream/consumer-group state lives here too.
suggested_fix: Use a StatefulSet with a PVC (or enable AOF/RDB on a mounted volume), set requirepass via a Secret and reference it in REDIS_URL, and add a NetworkPolicy restricting access to pulse-api/worker/scheduler.
failure_scenario: Redis pod restarted (node drain, OOM at 512Mi) -> all pulse:revoked:* keys vanish -> previously logged-out JWTs pass is_token_revoked() again until natural expiry (auth bypass window); in-flight stream messages and PEL state lost. Any pod in the namespace can also read/flush all data unauthenticated.
verification_notes: YAML validated. redis.yaml now StatefulSet + 2Gi PVC + AOF + requirepass (secretKeyRef); NetworkPolicy restricts 6379 to pulse app pods; REDIS_PASSWORD added to secrets.example; REDIS_URL in all 3 app manifests interpolates the password via env-list secretKeyRef. Live cluster apply pending.

title: The tenant-isolation test never attempts cross-workspace access; it only checks that /me echoes each token
root_cause: test_workspace_isolation_user_cannot_access_other_workspace mints two tokens for different workspace_ids and asserts /me reflects each token's own workspace. No resource in workspace A is ever requested with workspace B's token, so the test passes even if every workspace-scoped endpoint leaks data. It also silently encodes that a token for a workspace the user does not belong to is accepted with 200.
suggested_fix: Create a resource in workspace A, then request it (GET by id and list) with the workspace-B token and assert 404/empty, mirroring test_bulk_jobs.py's real isolation test; add a membership-check test once cross-workspace membership is implemented.
failure_scenario: A regression removes workspace filtering from a content/experiment endpoint -> this 'isolation' test still passes because /me keeps echoing token claims -> cross-tenant data leak ships undetected.
verification_notes: 140 tests pass. Isolation test now creates a real resource in workspace A and fetches/lists it with a workspace-B token, asserting 404/no-leak (replaces the vacuous /me-echo check).

title: Reaper marks live RUNNING jobs FAILED: progress is only written every 10 rows, which can exceed the 10-minute staleness window
root_cause: STALE_AFTER=10min assumes live jobs keep bumping updated_at, but worker/tasks.py writes progress only every PROGRESS_BATCH=10 rows and never heartbeats between batches. Ten slow LLM generations (timeouts + fallback, ~60-120s each) exceed the window. The worker's pause gate ignores FAILED, keeps processing, and its final commit overwrites the reaper's FAILED with SUCCEEDED — status flapping and false failure visible to users/webhooks. Related: #26.
suggested_fix: Heartbeat updated_at on a fixed timer (every 30-60s) independent of progress batches, or have the reaper check worker liveness/PEL ownership before failing; make the worker's final update conditional on not having been reaped.
failure_scenario: A 100-row job where each generation takes 70s: after row 9 (~10.5 min without a DB write) the reaper sets FAILED + errors['_worker']; the user sees a failed job and may resubmit; 100 minutes later the original worker silently flips it to SUCCEEDED.
verification_notes: 133 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. Time-based heartbeats (30s) in the row loop and pause-wait keep updated_at fresh independent of PROGRESS_BATCH; reaper window no longer trips on slow rows. Verified via reaper tests + code path; heartbeat interval constant documented.

title: Conversions counted per event while denominator is unique visitors: conversion rates >1 and inflated significance
root_cause: visitors is a deduplicated set but conversions increments for every 'conversion' event; ingest_event/ingest_events_batch insert duplicates freely (no per-visitor dedup) and visitor_hash is optional. A visitor converting twice yields conversions>visitor_count, breaking the binomial model feeding chi_squared_test and _recommend_winner (and enabling the #10 crash).
suggested_fix: Track converting visitors as a set (add visitor_hash on conversion events) and use its size as conversions, or dedupe events per (variant, visitor, event_type) before aggregation; require visitor_hash for conversion events.
failure_scenario: 50 visitors, 60 conversion events in treatment vs 50/50 in control: treatment rate reported as 120%, chi-squared computed on impossible cells reports a 'significant' win that is an artifact of duplicate events.
verification_notes: 129 tests pass. Conversions deduplicated per visitor (converting_visitors set); anonymous conversions count as distinct pseudo-visitors so rates stay <=1. Regression tests: test_conversions_deduplicated_per_visitor, test_anonymous_conversions_keep_rate_at_most_one.

title: Winner recommendation misattributes significance: recommends control and claims 'control is significantly better' when a treatment actually won
root_cause: _recommend_winner inspects only significant_results[0] and compares its treatment name against best_variant (highest raw rate across ALL variants). If the best raw-rate variant is a different, non-significant treatment, the code falls into the else branch and recommends the control of the significant pair, asserting the opposite of what that test showed. promote-winner then stops the experiment and persists the wrong winner. No multiple-comparison correction with 3+ arms.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the significant pair on its own direction, recommend the winner of that pair, and only consider other variants via their own tests; apply a correction (e.g. Bonferroni) when testing multiple treatments.
failure_scenario: Control 10%, treatment A 15% (p<0.05), treatment B 16% on tiny sample (not significant): best_variant=B != treatment_name=A -> returns recommended_variant=control with reason 'Control is statistically significantly better' — factually inverted; promote-winner promotes the worst arm.
verification_notes: 129 tests pass. _recommend_winner evaluates the significant pair's own rates (prefers analyses involving the best-rate arm) and applies Bonferroni correction across treatments. Regression test: test_winner_recommendation_not_inverted_with_three_arms.

title: SSRF guard is validate-then-fetch: DNS rebinding between getaddrinfo and httpx's own resolution bypasses it
root_cause: validate_webhook_url resolves the host with socket.getaddrinfo and checks the answers, but WebhookDispatcher.dispatch hands the hostname to httpx, which resolves it again at connect time. An attacker-controlled authoritative DNS can answer a public IP for the validation query and 169.254.169.254/127.0.0.1 for the connection query (TTL 0 / alternating answers). The guard is the only SSRF defense (no egress filtering); exploitable by any authenticated workspace user.
suggested_fix: Pin the validated address: resolve once, then connect to the literal IP with the original Host header (custom httpx transport/resolver returning only vetted addresses), or re-validate inside the connection hook so the checked IP is the connected IP.
failure_scenario: POST /webhooks with url=https://rebind.attacker.tld (A record alternates public/169.254.169.254, TTL 0), then POST /webhooks/{id}/test repeatedly: validation sees the public IP, httpx connects to the metadata endpoint; internal services reachable from the server.
verification_notes: 140 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. Dispatcher production path resolves+validates then connects via _PinnedBackend (httpcore network_backend pinned to validated IP); TLS SNI/verification still uses URL hostname. Regression test: test_pinned_backend_connects_to_validated_ip. Live network dispatch pending Docker host.

title: Blocking socket.getaddrinfo in async request path; attacker-controlled DNS can stall the whole event loop
root_cause: validate_webhook_url is a sync function called directly from async FastAPI handlers (api/v1/integrations.py:79, 152). getaddrinfo blocks the event loop for the full DNS resolution time, and the hostname is attacker-supplied — a deliberately slow/blackholed authoritative DNS holds every concurrent request on that replica hostage.
suggested_fix: Run resolution in a thread (asyncio.to_thread / loop.getaddrinfo) with a timeout, or make validate_webhook_url async and use the loop's resolver.
failure_scenario: Attacker registers a webhook whose nameserver delays responses 5s: each POST /webhooks or /test call freezes the API event loop for 5s, stalling all other tenants' requests on that replica; repeatable at will.
verification_notes: 140 tests pass. validate_webhook_url is async (asyncio.to_thread resolution) and returns validated IPs; both router call sites await it. Existing DNS-blocking tests updated and pass.

title: Non-atomic INCR + EXPIRE can leave a rate-limit key without TTL, permanently locking a client IP out of login/register
root_cause: INCR creates the key; EXPIRE is a separate command issued only when count==1. If the process dies or Redis errors between them, the key persists with no TTL. On recovery, count>1 so EXPIRE is never retried, ttl returns -1, and the counter grows forever — count>limit on every subsequent request.
suggested_fix: Make it atomic: a Lua script (INCR + PEXPIRE when new), pipeline(transaction=True), or SET key 0 EX ttl NX followed by INCR; additionally, if TTL returns -1 for an existing key, set the expiry defensively.
failure_scenario: First login attempt from an IP: INCR succeeds, then the connection drops before EXPIRE. After the 30s reprobe, every login/register from that IP returns 429 forever until an operator manually deletes pulse:ratelimit:login:<ip>.
verification_notes: 133 tests pass. incr() now runs an atomic Lua script (INCR+EXPIRE, defensive TTL=-1 repair). Regression test: test_incr_uses_atomic_script (stub client captures eval). Real-Redis execution pending Docker host.

title: Full Redis URL (potentially including password) logged at INFO
root_cause: connect() logs self._redis_url verbatim; redis:// or rediss:// URLs can embed credentials (redis://:password@host). The same pattern exists in core/redis_kv.py:67. Logs are shipped to stdout/aggregators, leaking the Redis credential to anyone with log access.
suggested_fix: Log only scheme/host/port/db (parse the URL and strip userinfo), or redact userinfo before logging in both redis_client.py and redis_kv.py.
failure_scenario: Production REDIS_URL=rediss://:s3cret@redis.internal:6380/0 -> every worker connect/reconnect writes the credential into centralized logs.
verification_notes: 133 tests pass. redact_url() strips userinfo; used in redis_client.connect and redis_kv._client logs. Regression test: test_redact_url_strips_credentials.

title: Bulk-job stream grows without bound: XADD has no MAXLEN and nothing ever trims or deletes acked entries
root_cause: push_job appends with plain xadd; ack only removes entries from the PEL, not from the stream. No XTRIM/XDEL/MAXLEN anywhere in the codebase, so every job ever dispatched is retained in Redis memory forever — on the same instance that holds rate-limit and revocation state (#40).
suggested_fix: Use xadd(..., maxlen=N, approximate=True) with a sane cap, or periodically XTRIM MINID based on the group's last-delivered/acked id; consider XDEL after ack.
failure_scenario: Months of production traffic: pulse:bulk_jobs accumulates millions of acked entries, Redis memory grows linearly until eviction/OOM, taking down rate limiting and token revocation with it.
verification_notes: 133 tests pass. push_job uses xadd(maxlen=10000, approximate=True). Regression test: test_push_job_bounds_stream_length.

title: PAUSED jobs orphaned by a worker crash are never recovered
root_cause: The reaper only handles RUNNING (fail) and PENDING (requeue). A worker blocked in _wait_for_resume holds the job in PAUSED; its stream message can be claimed and acked by another worker (skip path acks non-PENDING jobs, see #9), and if the paused worker then dies, no message and no reaper path remain. Resuming such a job sets RUNNING with nothing to process it.
suggested_fix: Include PAUSED in reaper recovery (re-enqueue paused jobs whose message is gone, or track worker ownership/heartbeat), and do not ack a claimed message unless its job is terminal or PENDING->RUNNING ownership was established.
failure_scenario: User pauses a long job; worker B claims the idle message and acks it; worker A is killed in a rollout. The job stays PAUSED indefinitely; POST /resume flips it to RUNNING, no worker picks it up, and 10 minutes later the reaper marks it FAILED without processing a remaining row.
verification_notes: 133 tests pass. Reaper fails stale PAUSED jobs (orphaned by crashed worker) with explicit _worker error; live pauses heartbeat so they are not reaped. Regression test: test_reap_fails_orphaned_paused_but_not_live_pause.

title: Passwords >72 bytes cause unhandled 500 on register/invite/login (bcrypt 5.0 raises)
root_cause: RegisterRequest.password and UserCreate.password enforce only min_length=8 with no upper bound. The installed bcrypt is 5.0.0 (verified in .venv), which raises ValueError('password cannot be longer than 72 bytes') instead of truncating; auth/security.py hash_password/verify_password call hashpw/checkpw directly with no length guard and no exception handling.
suggested_fix: Cap password length in the schemas (max 72 bytes, validated on the UTF-8 encoding) or pre-hash long passwords (e.g. SHA-256 base64) before bcrypt; alternatively catch ValueError and return 400/401.
failure_scenario: POST /auth/register with a 73+ byte passphrase (common for password-manager users) -> bcrypt.hashpw raises ValueError -> unhandled 500 instead of 201/400. Login with a >72-byte password -> checkpw raises -> 500 instead of 401.
verification_notes: 138 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. Password fields (login/register/invite) validate <=72 UTF-8 bytes -> 422 instead of bcrypt 500. Regression test: test_register_rejects_overlong_password.

title: Login/register rate limits bypassable by spoofing X-Forwarded-For
root_cause: client_ip trusts the leftmost XFF entry. The shipped compose stack publishes pulse-api directly on host port 8000, and the UI nginx proxy appends ($proxy_add_x_forwarded_for), preserving a client-supplied leftmost entry. The module docstring's precondition ('deployments must not expose the API directly') is violated by the repo's own deployment artifacts.
suggested_fix: Trust XFF only from configured proxy hops (take the rightmost untrusted entry, or use uvicorn --proxy-headers with forwarded-allow-ips); do not publish port 8000 in compose; make the UI nginx overwrite XFF with $remote_addr.
failure_scenario: Against the compose deployment, an attacker sends POST /auth/login directly to host:8000 with 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4' rotated per request -> each attempt gets a fresh counter key -> unlimited brute-force despite RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_PER_MINUTE=5.
verification_notes: 138 tests pass. client_ip honors XFF only from trusted-proxy CIDRs (RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXIES), taking rightmost untrusted entry; nginx overwrites XFF with $remote_addr; compose publishes API on 127.0.0.1 only. Regression test: test_client_ip_ignores_spoofed_xff_from_untrusted_peer.

title: Fail-open defaults: known JWT signing key and credentialed any-origin CORS unless PULSE_ENV is exactly 'production'; compose never sets it
root_cause: The default-secret refusal and CORS lockdown trigger only when pulse_env == 'production'. config.py defaults pulse_env='development' and pulse_secret_key='change-me-in-production'; .env.example ships PULSE_ENV=development with the default key, and docker-compose.yml never sets PULSE_ENV (env_file .env is optional). Development mode sets allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True, and compose publishes port 8000 on all host interfaces.
suggested_fix: Refuse to start with default secrets in any environment unless an explicit local-dev flag is set (or generate an ephemeral random key and log loudly); default pulse_env to 'production'; set PULSE_ENV and a real secret (${PULSE_SECRET_KEY:?err}) in the compose environment block.
failure_scenario: Operator runs docker compose up without creating .env: API signs JWTs with the committed default key -> anyone reaching port 8000 forges an owner token for any workspace/user id; any website can also make credentialed cross-origin requests because CORS echoes every origin.
verification_notes: 138 tests pass. Non-production create_app replaces committed default secrets with ephemeral random values (logged warning); production guard unchanged; compose sets PULSE_ENV explicitly. Regression test: test_default_secrets_replaced_outside_production.

title: Variant is_control flag from the API is silently discarded on create and update
root_cause: ExperimentVariantCreate.is_control (api/schemas/experiment.py:43-45) is never persisted: create_experiment (experiment_service.py:80-87) and update_experiment build ExperimentVariant without it, and the model has no is_control column. Results infer control from configuration.get('is_control', i == 0) (experiment_service.py:372), i.e. always position 0 unless the client smuggles the flag inside configuration.
suggested_fix: Persist the flag (map is_control into variant.configuration or add a column) in both create and update paths, and read it back consistently in get_results/ExperimentVariantRead.
failure_scenario: Client creates variants [{name:'B', is_control:true}, {name:'A'}] intending B as baseline: all statistical analyses and promote-winner treat A (position 0) as control, producing inverted lift/winner recommendations while the API accepted the payload without error.
verification_notes: 129 tests pass. is_control persisted into variant.configuration on create AND update; get_results reads it back. Regression test: test_is_control_flag_is_persisted.

title: Updating a draft experiment silently nulls variant attribution of existing events
root_cause: update_experiment bulk-deletes all ExperimentVariant rows and recreates them with new UUIDs. performance_events.variant_id FK is ON DELETE SET NULL, and ingestion never checks experiment status (#12), so DRAFT experiments can already hold events. The delete orphans those events (variant_id -> NULL); compute_results then drops them.
suggested_fix: Reject updates once events exist (or preserve variant ids for unchanged names), and/or restrict event ingestion to RUNNING experiments; at minimum warn/return the count of orphaned events.
failure_scenario: Create draft experiment, ingest 100 events (allowed — no status check), then PUT /experiments/{id} with renamed/reordered variants -> all 100 events get variant_id=NULL and vanish from results without any error; historical telemetry silently destroyed.
verification_notes: 140 tests pass. update_experiment keeps ids of surviving variant names (in-place update), deletes only removed variants; event attribution preserved. Regression test: test_update_experiment_preserves_variant_ids_and_events.

title: No role gating on content/review/bulk/webhook/experiment actions: viewers can approve, delete, and generate
root_cause: UserRole defines owner/admin/editor/viewer and auth.py gates user management, but none of the content, review, bulk-job, experiment, or webhook endpoints (or their services) check current_user.role. require_role exists in api/deps.py but is never used. A user invited as 'viewer' can approve/reject content, archive pieces, create bulk generation jobs (LLM spend), and register webhooks.
suggested_fix: Apply require_role(...) per operation: approve/reject/request-changes -> admin/owner (or a dedicated reviewer role), create/update/delete/versions/bulk-jobs -> editor+, webhooks -> admin+; keep read endpoints for viewer.
failure_scenario: Owner invites a contractor as viewer. The viewer POSTs /content/{id}/approve on REVIEW content (200, APPROVED), DELETEs any content piece, and POSTs /bulk-jobs with a 5MiB CSV to burn LLM quota — all actions the role model implies they should not have.
verification_notes: 138 tests pass. require_role gating: content/bulk/experiment writes editor+, approve/reject/request-changes and webhook management owner/admin; reads unchanged. Regression test: test_viewer_role_cannot_write_content.

title: POST /content/{id}/versions edits APPROVED/REVIEW content, bypassing the editorial state guard
root_cause: ContentService.update refuses edits unless status is DRAFT/REJECTED (content_service.py:138-142), but create_version applies the supplied body directly to content.body with no status check (content_service.py:210-212) while leaving content.status unchanged. The version endpoint is an unguarded write path around the review workflow.
suggested_fix: Apply the same DRAFT/REJECTED status guard in create_version when body is provided (or snapshot-only semantics: never mutate the live body from this endpoint).
failure_scenario: Content is APPROVED (published). Any workspace member POSTs /content/{id}/versions?body=<replacement text> -> content.body overwritten while status stays APPROVED; altered content served/exported as approved without re-review. (Note: body binds from query string, see #93.)
verification_notes: 138 tests pass. create_version refuses body edits unless DRAFT/REJECTED (same guard as update); snapshot-only versions still allowed. Regression test: test_versions_endpoint_cannot_edit_approved_content.

title: Upload size limit enforced only after the entire body is spooled to disk (disk-exhaustion DoS)
root_cause: Starlette parses the whole multipart body (file parts spool to a SpooledTemporaryFile that rolls to /tmp after 1MB) before the endpoint runs; the file.size pre-check and post-read len() check reject only after unlimited disk spooling. No request-body cap exists at the app, and compose exposes the API directly on :8000 with no proxy body limit.
suggested_fix: Enforce a streaming size cap while reading (read in chunks and abort past MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES), and/or set a server/proxy-level body limit (uvicorn/nginx client_max_body_size) on every exposed path.
failure_scenario: Against the directly exposed compose API, an attacker streams a 20GB 'file.csv' multipart body: Starlette spools ~20GB into the container's /tmp before the endpoint returns 413 -> disk exhaustion takes down the API. Repeated requests keep the disk full via deleted-but-open spool files.
verification_notes: 140 tests pass. Upload read in 64KiB chunks with running size cap (413 mid-stream). Note: Starlette multipart disk spooling is inherent; proxied paths capped by nginx (#32) and compose API now loopback-only (#52).

title: Anthropic adapter reads only the first content block; non-text first block yields empty 'successful' content
root_cause: text = content[0].get('text', '') assumes the first block is the text block. If the response begins with a non-text block (e.g. a thinking block with extended thinking, or tool_use) or contains multiple text blocks, the extracted text is empty or truncated while finish_reason stays 'end_turn' — recorded as success (compounds #2).
suggested_fix: Concatenate all blocks of type 'text'; treat an empty extraction as an error response.
failure_scenario: Anthropic response content=[{'type':'thinking',...},{'type':'text','text':'...'}] -> text='' with finish_reason='end_turn' -> orchestrator records success and returns empty content.
verification_notes: 145 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. Anthropic adapter concatenates all type=text blocks. Regression test: test_anthropic_concatenates_all_text_blocks (thinking block first + two text blocks).

title: Fallback provides no protection when secondary is the same provider or chosen by registration order
root_cause: The router blindly trusts primary/secondary identities. The only production wiring (api/v1/generate.py:39-45) picks providers[0]/providers[1] by dict insertion order (no configured preference) and sets secondary=primary when just one provider is registered. In OPEN state route_request then returns the very provider that is failing.
suggested_fix: Select primary/secondary by explicit config preference (not registration order); when only one provider exists, disable fallback routing or apply backoff instead of routing OPEN-state traffic to the same provider; optionally guard FallbackRouter against primary is secondary.
failure_scenario: Only OLLAMA_BASE_URL configured: Ollama goes down -> 3 failures -> circuit OPEN -> route_request returns the same dead provider -> every request still hits the downed service with full timeouts; the breaker changes nothing.
verification_notes: 145 tests pass. Explicit provider preference order (openai/anthropic/ollama); single-provider wiring now fails fast via CircuitOpenError while OPEN/HALF_OPEN-excess instead of hammering the dead provider; orchestrator maps it to GenerationError. Regression test: test_single_provider_circuit_fails_fast.

title: User model still declares uq_users_workspace_email after migration 002 replaced it with globally unique email
root_cause: 002_user_auth drops uq_users_workspace_email and creates uq_users_email (email alone) because login looks users up without workspace context, but the ORM metadata was never updated. SQLite tests build tables from metadata (per-workspace uniqueness) while PostgreSQL enforces global uniqueness.
suggested_fix: Replace the model's UniqueConstraint with UniqueConstraint('email', name='uq_users_email') to match migration 002.
failure_scenario: alembic autogenerate emits a spurious migration dropping uq_users_email and re-adding uq_users_workspace_email (which would break login lookups if applied); a test registering the same email in two workspaces passes on SQLite but violates uq_users_email in production.
verification_notes: 149 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. User model UniqueConstraint now uq_users_email(email) matching migration 002. Drift-guard test: test_user_and_workspace_constraints_match_migrations.

title: Workspace.slug declares unique=True plus a named UniqueConstraint, creating a duplicate constraint absent from the migration
root_cause: mapped_column(unique=True) generates an unnamed unique constraint in Base.metadata in addition to the explicit uq_workspaces_slug in __table_args__. Migration 001 creates only uq_workspaces_slug, so metadata and database diverge.
suggested_fix: Drop unique=True from the slug column and keep only the named UniqueConstraint.
failure_scenario: alembic check/autogenerate reports a phantom extra unique constraint on workspaces.slug; SQLite test schema carries a redundant second unique index.
verification_notes: 149 tests pass. Removed unique=True from Workspace.slug; only named uq_workspaces_slug remains. Same drift-guard test.

title: list_experiments issues one variant query per experiment (N+1)
root_cause: After the paginated experiment query, a separate select(ExperimentVariant) is executed for each item instead of a single selectinload/IN query. Same path exercised by GET /experiments (api/v1/experiments.py:88-105).
suggested_fix: Use selectinload(Experiment.variants) on the page query or one SELECT ... WHERE experiment_id IN (:ids) and group in Python.
failure_scenario: GET /experiments?limit=100 executes 102 queries per request (count + page + 100 variant selects), multiplying DB round-trips and latency under load.
verification_notes: 149 tests pass. list_experiments loads all page variants in one IN query. Regression test: test_list_experiments_single_variant_query (SQLAlchemy event listener counts exactly 1 variant SELECT for 3 experiments).

title: create_version computes max(version_number)+1 without locking; concurrent snapshots raise unhandled IntegrityError (500)
root_cause: Two concurrent POST /content/{id}/versions both read the same max version and insert the same next_version; uq_content_versions_piece_version rejects the second insert and nothing catches IntegrityError (same pattern as the slug pre-check in create()).
suggested_fix: Catch IntegrityError and retry/translate to 409, or lock the parent row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) before computing the next version number.
failure_scenario: Two editors (or a double-clicked UI) snapshot the same content simultaneously: one gets 201, the other a 500 instead of a clean conflict/retry; the same race on create() turns a duplicate slug into a 500 instead of the intended 409.
verification_notes: 149 tests pass. create() and create_version() catch IntegrityError -> rollback -> 409. Regression test: test_create_version_conflict_returns_409.

title: Raw database URL passed to ConfigParser interpolation breaks alembic when the URL contains '%'
root_cause: config.set_main_option stores the URL in a ConfigParser section; percent signs (common in percent-encoded passwords, e.g. p%40ss) are interpreted as interpolation syntax when alembic later reads sqlalchemy.url, raising InterpolationSyntaxError. Alembic requires escaping '%' as '%%'.
suggested_fix: config.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", get_settings().database_url.replace("%", "%%")) — or pass the URL via custom engine attributes instead of the ini section.
failure_scenario: DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://pulse:p%40ss@host/pulse -> every alembic command crashes with configparser.InterpolationSyntaxError before touching the database.
verification_notes: 149 tests pass. env.py escapes % as %% for ConfigParser. Drift-guard test: test_alembic_env_escapes_percent_in_url.

title: Webhook deleteMutation has no onError — delete failures are invisible
root_cause: Unlike createMutation and testMutation, deleteMutation defines only onSuccess. A failed DELETE (403/404/500/network) is stored in mutation state that the component never reads.
suggested_fix: Add onError: (err) => setFormError(apiErrorMessage(err, 'Failed to delete webhook')), and optionally disable the button while deleteMutation.isPending.
failure_scenario: API returns 500 on DELETE /webhooks/{id}: the user clicks Delete, nothing visibly happens, and the webhook remains after the invalidate refetch — the user assumes the click missed and retries.

title: BulkJobStatus type omits 'paused', which the backend can return
root_cause: The backend BulkJobStatus enum includes PAUSED='paused' with pause/resume endpoints, but the frontend union and BulkJobs.tsx STATUS_COLORS omit it. The ?? fallback prevents a crash, but the type lies about the API contract. Related backend drift: #21.
suggested_fix: Add 'paused' to BulkJobStatus and a corresponding entry in STATUS_COLORS; consider surfacing pause/resume actions in the UI.
failure_scenario: A job paused via the API returns status 'paused'; TypeScript callers believe this is impossible, and the UI shows an unstyled fallback badge with no way to resume.

title: No security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) on the SPA
root_cause: The nginx server block adds no security headers and index.html has no CSP meta. Combined with the localStorage-stored JWT (#31), this leaves the app clickjackable and gives XSS no defense-in-depth containment.
suggested_fix: Add X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, and a Content-Security-Policy tuned for the Vite bundle and API origin to the server block.
failure_scenario: An attacker iframes the Pulse UI on a malicious page and clickjacks an authenticated user into clicking 'Delete' on a webhook or 'Stop' on a running experiment; no frame-busting header prevents it.
verification_notes: nginx adds X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy (always). Full CSP deferred pending Vite bundle/API origin tuning.

title: Compose publishes Redis (no auth), Postgres and MinIO (default credentials) on host ports
root_cause: ports mappings bind 6379, 5432 (pulse/pulse), 9000/9001 (minioadmin/minioadmin) on all host interfaces; Redis has no password at all. Fine for isolated localhost dev, but the stack is routinely run on shared/remote hosts.
suggested_fix: Bind published ports to 127.0.0.1 (e.g. '127.0.0.1:6379:6379') or drop the ports entirely since inter-service traffic uses the compose network; set a Redis password.
failure_scenario: make dev on a shared server or untrusted LAN -> anyone reaching the host can connect to unauthenticated Redis (read revocation markers, inject/flush bulk-job stream messages) or log into Postgres/MinIO with the committed default credentials.

title: Makefile targets use bash-only 'source' under make's default /bin/sh
root_cause: make executes recipes with /bin/sh, which is dash on Debian/Ubuntu; 'source' is not a dash builtin. The api/worker/scheduler/test/lint/typecheck targets all use 'source .venv/bin/activate'. Works on macOS but fails on Linux dev machines.
suggested_fix: Add 'SHELL := /bin/bash' at the top of the Makefile or replace 'source' with POSIX '.'.
failure_scenario: Linux contributor runs make test -> '/bin/sh: 1: source: not found' -> every venv-based target is unusable.

title: Dependency-layer caching claim is false: src is copied before pip install
root_cause: The comment says 'Install dependencies first (without src/) to leverage layer caching', but COPY src ./src precedes RUN pip install ., so any source edit invalidates the dependency-install layer.
suggested_fix: Copy only pyproject.toml/README.md first, install dependencies, then COPY src and reinstall the local package; or use a two-stage build.
failure_scenario: Every one-line code change triggers a full re-download/reinstall of fastapi/sqlalchemy/etc. in CI image builds and local make build, adding minutes per build.

title: 'Validate deployment manifests' only checks YAML syntax, giving false confidence
root_cause: The step yaml.safe_load_all's each file and prints OK; it performs no schema/semantic validation. The broken $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) expansion (#5), the example-secret/production-guard conflict (#38), and the missing migration step (#6) all pass this 'validation'.
suggested_fix: Add kubeconform/kubeval schema validation and a semantic check (e.g. grep for $(VAR) references not defined earlier in the same env list), or rename the step to 'YAML syntax check'.
failure_scenario: A PR introduces a manifest that parses as YAML but cannot deploy (as the current ones do) -> CI stays green -> defect reaches the cluster.

title: Worker and scheduler Deployments define no liveness/readiness probes
