root_cause: pulse-worker.yaml and pulse-scheduler.yaml containers have env/resources only. A hung process keeps the pod 'Running' forever; kubelet never restarts it. The worker's Redis-reconnect loop does not cover hangs inside job processing (e.g. the #4 deadlock).
suggested_fix: Add a liveness probe (exec check of a heartbeat file the loop touches, or an HTTP health/metrics endpoint) and a readiness signal for both Deployments.
failure_scenario: Worker pod deadlocks on a stalled DB connection -> pod stays Ready/Running -> bulk jobs stop being consumed and only the scheduler reaper notices after the staleness window; with the scheduler itself hung, nothing recovers.

title: PULSE_API_HOST / PULSE_API_PORT are advertised but read by nothing
root_cause: config.py defines pulse_api_host/pulse_api_port, but no consumer exists: the Dockerfile CMD and Makefile hardcode --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000, and k8s/compose set the port independently.
suggested_fix: Either honor the settings in the uvicorn invocation (entrypoint script) or remove the variables from config.py/.env.example/configmap to avoid misleading operators.
failure_scenario: Operator sets PULSE_API_PORT=9000 expecting the API to move -> container still listens on 8000 -> healthchecks/proxies pointed at 9000 fail.

title: Readiness endpoint always returns ok; k8s readiness probe is meaningless
root_cause: /health/ready (used by k8s/pulse-api.yaml readinessProbe) returns a static {'status':'ok'} without checking DB/Redis connectivity, so pods receive traffic while their dependencies are down.
suggested_fix: Perform a cheap SELECT 1 (and optional Redis PING) with a short timeout in readiness; return 503 on failure. Keep /health/live static.
failure_scenario: Postgres fails over; API pods stay 'Ready' and keep receiving requests; every DB-backed call 500s instead of traffic being held until connections recover.
verification_notes: 163 tests pass. /health/ready pings DB (SELECT 1, 2s timeout) once engine initialized; 503 on failure; skipped pre-init. Regression tests: test_readiness_503_when_db_down + isolated test_readiness.

title: test_list_users_requires_admin only exercises the positive (owner) path
root_cause: The test creates a viewer user but never authenticates as that viewer; it only asserts the owner gets 201/200. The role-gating negative case (viewer/editor must get 403 on GET/POST /auth/users) is untested anywhere in the suite.
suggested_fix: Log in as the created viewer (or mint a viewer token) and assert 403 on GET /api/v1/auth/users and POST /api/v1/auth/users.
failure_scenario: A refactor drops the admin/owner dependency from the user-management router -> suite stays green -> any viewer can enumerate and create users in the workspace.

title: test_update_content_status never updates a status
root_cause: Despite the name/docstring, the test only creates content and filters the list by status=draft. No PUT with a status field is issued and no status transition is asserted.
suggested_fix: PUT a status change (or remove the misleading test and rely on the review-workflow tests), and assert the returned/persisted status.
failure_scenario: PUT /content/{id} silently ignores or mishandles the status field -> this test still passes -> status-update regression goes unnoticed.

title: test_ingest_event_updates_variant_metrics never checks any metric
root_cause: The test ingests 26 events and asserts only 201 on each POST; it never reads variant metrics/results to verify impressions/conversions were actually recorded.
suggested_fix: After ingestion, GET /api/v1/experiments/{id}/results and assert impression/conversion counts match the ingested numbers.
failure_scenario: Event ingestion starts returning 201 but drops events (wrong variant_id mapping or failed commit) -> this test passes -> experiment metrics silently stay zero.

title: Storage upload/download test uses a mock transport that masks the unauthenticated S3 request
root_cause: StorageClient.upload_file sends a plain PUT with no Authorization/SigV4 header and download_file is likewise unsigned (#85). The test queues canned 200 responses and never inspects the outgoing request for auth, so it cannot detect that real MinIO/S3 would reject every upload with 403.
suggested_fix: Assert the recorded request carries a valid signature (once implemented), or add a test against a real MinIO container; at minimum assert on transport.requests so the missing auth is visible.
failure_scenario: Someone wires StorageClient into an export/asset flow -> tests stay green -> every upload against the compose MinIO (which requires auth) fails with 403 AccessDenied in production.

title: In-process fallback test relies on a 50ms sleep, making it timing-flaky
root_cause: test_create_bulk_job_falls_back_to_in_process waits for the background fallback task with 'await asyncio.sleep(0.05)' instead of synchronizing on the task; under CI load the task may not have run within 50ms.
suggested_fix: Expose/await the created task (capture it via the monkeypatched _run_in_process with an asyncio.Event, or await pending tasks) instead of sleeping.
failure_scenario: Slow/loaded CI runner -> fallback task hasn't appended to 'processed' within 50ms -> assertion fails intermittently, eroding trust in the suite.

title: app_fixture rebuilds a private FastAPI app instead of using pulse.main.create_app
root_cause: The fixture constructs its own FastAPI() with different CORS settings and re-includes routers manually, so nearly all API tests run against an app that can diverge from production wiring (middleware order, the production default-secret guard, root health routes absent). Only test_health.py imports the real app. This is a root cause of the production-wiring defects (#1, #53) going undetected.
suggested_fix: Build the fixture from pulse.main.create_app() (with test settings) and apply dependency_overrides to it, so router/middleware wiring regressions are caught.
failure_scenario: A change to main.py drops or misorders a middleware/router -> all fixture-based tests still pass against the hand-built app -> production app is broken while CI is green.

title: Floating-point cumulative boundary gives off-by-one bucket allocation; granularity is %100, not the documented %10000
root_cause: bucket < cumulative*100 with float weights: e.g. weight 0.07 yields cumulative*100 = 7.000000000000001, so bucket 7 is assigned to the 7% variant (8 buckets instead of 7). Also hash_int % 100 contradicts CLAUDE.md/TSD's %10000 design, so sub-1% weights cannot be represented at all.
suggested_fix: Use integer basis points: bucket = hash_int % 10000 and cumulative weights scaled to integers (round(normalized*10000)) with the last variant taking the remainder.
failure_scenario: assign_variant(v, e, {'a': 0.07, 'b': 0.93}): visitors hashing to bucket 7 get 'a' although 'a' should own exactly buckets 0-6 — systematic 1% traffic misallocation for any weight whose float product rounds up.
verification_notes: 145 tests pass. Assignment uses %10000 buckets with integer basis-point cumulative weights (_assign_bucket); last variant takes remainder. Regression test: test_assignment_uses_integer_basis_points (boundaries + sub-1% weights).

title: Event properties can overwrite the Mixpanel project token
root_cause: properties is seeded with {'token': self._project_token, ...} and then properties.update(event.get('properties', {})) lets any event property named 'token' replace the credential. (Connector currently has no call sites, so this is latent.)
suggested_fix: Apply event properties first, then force token/distinct_id/source afterwards, or strip reserved keys from event properties.
failure_scenario: An event whose properties include {'token': '<other-project-token>'} is imported into a different Mixpanel project (or rejected), corrupting analytics attribution once the connector is wired up.

title: Analytics send() ignores HTTP response status: failed deliveries are silently lost
root_cause: GA4 send posts without raise_for_status or any status check; Mixpanel (mixpanel.py:62-65) and Segment (segment.py:50-54) share the pattern. 4xx/5xx responses are treated as success. Latent today (no call sites), but defeats the purpose once wired.
suggested_fix: Call response.raise_for_status() (or check status and log/count failures) in all three connectors; consider bounded retry for 5xx.
failure_scenario: GA4 api_secret rotated/expired -> every POST returns 403 -> send() returns normally, callers believe events were delivered, and all analytics data is silently dropped.

title: Presigned URL signs the raw key while the request path is percent-encoded; upload/download send no authentication at all
root_cause: _sign builds string_to_sign with the unencoded key but _object_url percent-encodes it, so for keys with spaces/unicode/+ the signature won't match the canonical resource S3/MinIO computes. Additionally upload_file/download_file PUT/GET without any Authorization header, so they only work against public buckets. Latent: no call sites yet — but #7's recommended fix routes bulk payloads through this client.
suggested_fix: Sign the same encoded resource that appears in the URL (or implement SigV4 properly), and add request signing to upload_file/download_file before this client is used against private buckets.
failure_scenario: get_presigned_url('report final.csv') -> URL path /bucket/report%20final.csv but signature computed over '/bucket/report final.csv' -> S3/MinIO returns 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch; upload_file to a private bucket returns 403 AccessDenied.

title: Tracking-URL generation silently drops repeated and blank query parameters from the base URL
root_cause: parse_qs returns lists but the code keeps only v[0] per key, and parse_qs defaults to keep_blank_values=False. A base URL like ?tag=a&tag=b&ref= loses tag=b and ref entirely when the tracking URL is rebuilt.
suggested_fix: Preserve multi-values with parse_qs(..., keep_blank_values=True) and urlencode(doseq=True), updating only the UTM/experiment keys.
failure_scenario: generate_tracking_url('https://x.com/p?tag=a&tag=b&ref=', ...) returns a URL with only tag=a and no ref — downstream attribution/campaign parameters corrupted.
verification_notes: 145 tests pass. parse_qs(keep_blank_values=True) + urlencode(doseq=True) preserve repeated/blank params. Regression test: test_tracking_url_preserves_repeated_and_blank_params.

title: Dead-letter attempt count is read before XAUTOCLAIM increments it (off-by-one), and pending counts are capped at 1000
root_cause: pending_delivery_counts is fetched before claim_stale, but XAUTOCLAIM increments times_delivered, so attempts lags the true delivery count by one — a message is processed one extra time beyond max_attempts before dead-lettering. Also xpending_range count=1000 (worker/redis_client.py:131-137) without pagination means messages beyond the first 1000 PEL entries default to attempts=1 and can evade the dead-letter threshold.
suggested_fix: Use counts.get(message_id, 0) + 1 (post-claim semantics) or re-read XPENDING after claiming; paginate xpending_range until exhausted.
failure_scenario: max_attempts=5: a poison job is delivered 7 times before dead-lettering instead of 6; with >1000 pending messages, deep-PEL entries always look like first attempts and are retried indefinitely.
verification_notes: 145 tests pass. pending_delivery_counts paginates XPENDING until exhausted; claimed-message attempts = pre-claim count + 1 (post-XAUTOCLAIM semantics). Regression test: test_pending_delivery_counts_paginates (1001 entries across 2 pages).

title: claim_stale discards the XAUTOCLAIM cursor and always restarts at 0-0 with count=10
root_cause: The returned next-start cursor is ignored, so every recovery sweep rescans the PEL from the beginning. In Redis 7 COUNT bounds the number of PEL entries scanned, so if the first 10 PEL entries are fresh (actively processing deliveries), stale entries behind them are never reached.
suggested_fix: Persist and pass the returned cursor across sweeps (reset to 0-0 only when it returns 0-0), and/or raise count; alternatively iterate XPENDING to target known-stale ids.
failure_scenario: 12 messages pending: 10 recently delivered at the PEL head, 2 crashed-consumer messages behind them. Every _recover_pending scans only the first 10 (all fresh) and claims nothing; the orphaned messages wait until the head drains.
verification_notes: 163 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. claim_stale persists the XAUTOCLAIM cursor across sweeps (reset on 0-0 wrap). Regression test: test_claim_stale_persists_cursor.

title: Comment claims stdlib logging is routed through structlog, but basicConfig leaves stdlib logs as plain text
root_cause: structlog.configure only affects structlog loggers; logging.basicConfig(format='%(message)s') does not attach a structlog ProcessorFormatter, so logging.getLogger(__name__) calls (worker dispatch, tasks, maintenance, bulk_jobs API) emit unstructured lines, contrary to the comment and the repo's structured-logging convention.
suggested_fix: Route stdlib records through structlog via logging.config.dictConfig with a ProcessorFormatter handler (foreign_pre_chain matching the configured processors), or convert stdlib loggers to structlog.
failure_scenario: Log aggregation expecting JSON gets plain-text lines from pulse.worker.dispatch while pulse-worker emits JSON — parsing/alerting on those events silently fails.
verification_notes: 163 tests pass. stdlib records routed through structlog ProcessorFormatter (JSON). Regression test: test_stdlib_logging_rendered_as_json.

title: Blocking CSV file I/O inside the async worker loop
root_cause: _read_input_csv (and _write_output_csv at 227-231) perform synchronous file reads/writes directly in the coroutine, blocking the event loop for the duration of the I/O (up to a 5 MiB upload, larger outputs). In the in-process API fallback this stalls all concurrent HTTP requests.
suggested_fix: Wrap file reads/writes in asyncio.to_thread, or stream rows incrementally instead of materializing the whole CSV.
failure_scenario: In-process fallback (Redis down): a 5 MiB CSV read plus a large output write on a slow disk blocks the API event loop for hundreds of milliseconds per job, stalling health checks and other tenants' requests.
verification_notes: 158 tests pass. _read_input_csv/_write_output_csv run via asyncio.to_thread in the worker loop.

title: New Redis connection (plus ensure_group round-trip) per enqueued job
root_cause: enqueue_job constructs a fresh RedisClient, connects, ensures the group, pushes one job, and disconnects on every call. The reaper loops enqueue_job per stale job, so a sweep of N jobs pays N connection setups and 3N round-trips.
suggested_fix: Reuse a module-level/shared client (as redis_kv does) or accept an injected client; call ensure_group once at startup rather than per enqueue.
failure_scenario: Scheduler reaper requeues 200 backlog jobs after a Redis outage: 200 TCP+AUTH handshakes and 600 round-trips in a tight loop, slowing recovery and spiking Redis connection churn.
verification_notes: 158 tests pass. dispatch keeps a shared RedisClient (connect once, ensure_group once); broken client dropped for reconnect. Regression test: test_enqueue_reuses_shared_client (1 connect for 2 enqueues).

title: ContentRead/ContentVersionRead serialize 'metadata_' instead of 'metadata' (alias leaks into responses; frontend type disagrees)
root_cause: Field(alias='metadata_') sets both validation and serialization alias; FastAPI serializes response models by_alias=True by default, so the JSON key is 'metadata_' (also line 87 for ContentVersionRead). The frontend types declare 'metadata' (pulse-ui/src/types/index.ts:41,53), so the public API contract exposes the internal column name and the TS contract is untruthful.
suggested_fix: Use validation_alias=AliasChoices('metadata_', 'metadata') with serialization kept at 'metadata' (or Field(validation_alias='metadata_') plus populate_by_name); align the TS types with whichever wire key is chosen.
failure_scenario: GET /content/{id} returns {'metadata_': {...}}; any client (including the shipped TS types) reading response.metadata gets undefined — metadata silently appears missing.
verification_notes: 155 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. ContentRead/ContentVersionRead use validation_alias only; responses now serialize 'metadata' (matches TS types). Regression test: test_content_response_serializes_metadata_not_metadata_.

title: POST /content/{id}/versions takes body/change_note as query parameters, silently ignoring a JSON body
root_cause: body and change_note are plain scalar parameters with defaults and no Body(...) annotation, so FastAPI binds them from the query string. Clients POSTing the natural JSON payload {body, change_note} are ignored without error.
suggested_fix: Declare a Pydantic request model (VersionCreate) or annotate the scalars with Body(...); document the contract.
failure_scenario: Client POSTs /content/{id}/versions with JSON {'body': 'new text'} -> FastAPI reads body=None from query -> creates a snapshot of the OLD body and never applies the intended edit, returning 201 as if it succeeded.
verification_notes: 155 tests pass. New VersionCreate pydantic body model; JSON payload honored (query-only binding removed). Regression test: test_versions_accepts_json_body; #57 guard test updated to JSON.

title: Annotation action is an unvalidated free-text field, allowing approval-chain spoofing
root_cause: ReviewAction is a bare str subclass used as a namespace, and AnnotationCreate.action accepts any string; review_service.add_annotation stores it verbatim. get_approval_chain renders these actions as workflow steps, so a user can inject 'approved'/'submitted' steps that never corresponded to a real state transition.
suggested_fix: Constrain action to a Literal/enum of annotation-safe values (e.g. 'annotated', 'commented') and reject workflow-transition actions on this endpoint.
failure_scenario: Viewer POSTs /content/{id}/annotations {action:'approved', comment:'LGTM'} -> 201; GET /content/{id}/approval-chain shows an 'approved' step by that user although the piece is still in REVIEW, misleading auditors.
verification_notes: 155 tests pass. AnnotationCreate.action constrained to Literal['annotated','commented']; workflow actions rejected 422. Regression test: test_annotation_rejects_workflow_action_spoofing.

title: Over-broad 'does not exist' substring match fails open on user validation
root_cause: Any ProgrammingError/OperationalError whose message contains 'does not exist' (e.g. 'column users.is_active does not exist' after a partial migration) is treated as 'users table not migrated' and the token claims pass unvalidated — disabling the existence/is_active checks for deactivated or deleted users.
suggested_fix: Match only the specific undefined-table condition for the users table (SQLSTATE 42P01 / sqlite 'no such table: users'), not arbitrary substrings; fail closed (503) otherwise.
failure_scenario: A deployment runs migration 001 but not 002 (users.is_active missing): every request with a validly signed token hits 'column ... does not exist' -> validation skipped -> a deactivated user's unexpired token keeps full access instead of 403.
verification_notes: 155 tests pass. Fail-open limited to SQLSTATE 42P01 / 'no such table: users'; missing-column errors now 503. Regression tests: test_missing_column_error_does_not_fail_open, test_missing_users_table_still_fails_open.

title: Missing/malformed JWT claims raise KeyError/ValueError -> 500 instead of 401
root_cause: After signature validation, payload['sub'], payload['workspace_id'], payload['email'], payload['role'] are accessed with [] and uuid.UUID() without try/except; a signed token lacking these claims crashes the dependency.
suggested_fix: Wrap claim extraction in try/except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) and raise HTTPException 401 'Invalid token claims'.
failure_scenario: A request presents a correctly HS256-signed token whose payload lacks 'workspace_id' (foreign issuer reusing the secret) -> KeyError propagates -> 500 with stack trace in logs instead of a clean 401.
verification_notes: 155 tests pass. Claim extraction wrapped (KeyError/ValueError/TypeError -> 401). Regression test: test_token_missing_claims_returns_401.

title: Blocking file I/O (write_bytes / Path.exists) in async bulk-job endpoints
root_cause: create_bulk_job writes up to 5MiB with synchronous Path.write_bytes, and download_bulk_job_results stats the output path synchronously (line 240), both on the event loop.
suggested_fix: Use anyio.to_thread.run_sync / aiofiles for the write and existence check (or stream the upload to disk in chunks).
failure_scenario: Several concurrent 5MiB uploads on a slow filesystem block the loop for the duration of each write, stalling all other requests including health probes.
verification_notes: 158 tests pass, ruff/mypy clean. Upload write and download stat run via asyncio.to_thread; existing upload/download tests exercise the paths.

title: Fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task without a strong reference (task may be GC'd mid-job)
root_cause: The in-process fallback task is created but never stored; asyncio only keeps weak references to tasks, so a garbage-collection pass can cancel the running bulk job. A GC'd task dies silently and the job stays RUNNING until the reaper fails it.
suggested_fix: Keep a module-level set of background tasks (add on create, discard via add_done_callback), or use a supervised task group.
failure_scenario: Redis down at dispatch time -> fallback task created; under memory pressure a GC cycle collects the unreferenced task mid-processing -> job silently stops at partial progress and is later reaped as FAILED with no error recorded.
verification_notes: 158 tests pass. Module-level _background_tasks set holds fallback tasks; done-callback discards. Regression test: test_fallback_task_holds_strong_reference.

title: Client-supplied filename used unsanitized in filesystem path (500s on crafted names)
root_cause: Only the '.csv' suffix is checked; the raw filename is concatenated into the storage path. Names containing '/' or null bytes produce invalid/unwritable paths (nested dirs don't exist -> FileNotFoundError; '\0' -> ValueError), surfacing as unhandled 500s. Traversal writes are blocked only incidentally by the glued UUID prefix plus missing intermediate dirs.
suggested_fix: Sanitize with Path(filename).name, strip/replace path separators and control characters, and wrap the write in try/except returning 400 cleanly.
failure_scenario: POST /bulk-jobs with filename='a/b.csv' -> path _UPLOAD_DIR/'<uuid>_a/b.csv' -> parent dir missing -> FileNotFoundError -> 500 instead of 400; filename containing a null byte -> ValueError -> 500.
verification_notes: 158 tests pass. Filename sanitized via Path().name + printable filter; write OSError -> 400. Regression test: test_upload_filename_with_separator_is_sanitized.

title: Middleware-order comment states the opposite of Starlette's actual behavior
root_cause: The comment claims 'first added = outermost', but Starlette's add_middleware inserts at position 0 so the LAST added middleware is outermost — here TenantMiddleware wraps CORSMiddleware. Harmless today only because TenantMiddleware is a no-op; any future enforcement in it would run before CORS and break preflight OPTIONS handling.
suggested_fix: Correct the comment and add TenantMiddleware before CORSMiddleware (so CORS is outermost), or drop the no-op middleware entirely.
failure_scenario: A developer adds workspace enforcement to TenantMiddleware trusting the comment; browser preflight OPTIONS requests (no Authorization header) are rejected before CORSMiddleware can answer them, breaking all cross-origin UI calls.
verification_notes: 163 tests pass. TenantMiddleware added before CORS so CORS is outermost; comment corrected. Regression test: test_cors_middleware_is_outermost.

title: Concurrent first requests create multiple Redis clients; losers leak unclosed
root_cause: _client() has no lock: N coroutines arriving while _redis is None each build a client and ping; the last assignment wins and the other N-1 clients (with open connection pools) are dropped without aclose().
suggested_fix: Guard creation with an asyncio.Lock, or close the previous client when replacing it.
failure_scenario: API startup burst of 50 concurrent logins with Redis reachable -> up to 50 clients created, 49 abandoned with live connections -> connection leak against Redis maxclients until GC/finalizers run.
verification_notes: 163 tests pass. RedisKV._client creation guarded by asyncio.Lock with double-check. Regression test: test_kv_client_creation_is_serialized (10 concurrent calls -> 1 client).

title: .gitignore ignores venv/ and env/ but not .venv/ — the directory name the project's own setup instructions use
root_cause: CLAUDE.md documents 'source .venv/bin/activate', but the Python section of .gitignore lists only venv/ and env/. Nothing is mis-committed today, but a future git add -A could stage the entire virtualenv.
suggested_fix: Add '.venv/' to the Python section of .gitignore.
failure_scenario: Contributor follows CLAUDE.md, creates .venv/, runs git add -A -> thousands of virtualenv files staged/committed, bloating the repo and leaking local paths.
verification_notes: .gitignore now ignores .venv/ (the name CLAUDE.md setup uses) and k8s/secrets.yaml.
